lines.text: Ben planted his trekking pole on a smooth rock slab, leaned his weight on it,
and the metal tip skidded right out from under him.
On bare rock, pavement and boardwalks, push a rubber tip onto each pole.
It grips hard surfaces and stops the clicking and scratching.
On mud, snow and ice, pull it off so the metal tip bites.
Save this before your next rocky hike.
